search_strategy: Systematic bulk-dump-then-grep, not per-remark exploration. The agent: (1) dumped all 114 BookStack wiki pages with their HTML bodies AND comments to /tmp/wiki via the API (line 977-983) -- a good technique that DID make the PLAN_FILE_NAME comment reachable in principle -- but then relied on narrow keyword greps ('planner', 'payload', 'batch size') across that dump rather than opening every page its own greps flagged as relevant; page 7 (the one design doc that actually discusses the planner) surfaced in two separate grep results (lines 1294, 1303) and was never opened, leading the agent to wrongly conclude 'Wiki doesn't have the planner design' (line 1381) and abandon the wiki entirely. (2) Dumped all Mattermost channels to /tmp/chat and ran dozens of targeted greps (plan_id, plan_format_version, sha256, sweep, stale, etc.) -- this was thorough and recovered the large majority of the design (31 of 42 clues, all 4 reversals, 1 of 4 herrings). (3) Dumped the full IMAP mailbox to /tmp/mail (line 1734) and grepped for 'planner|plan_batches|PlannedBatch|payload' -- this missed g1.r2.l6 because that thread's subject/body never uses those exact tokens. (4) Also dumped all 736 Gitea issues with comments (line 1432-1433) though issue #691 'feat: auto batch mode' does not appear to have been the load-bearing source for any graded fact. Overall the agent reconstructed the design almost completely correctly (correct envelope order, correct fingerprint algorithm and golden digests, correct sweep-after-plan ordering, correct metadata exclusion) but lost 4 of 10 facts to two narrow, avoidable gaps: one wiki page never opened despite being flagged twice, and one motivating incident (the 600-row/5000-byte ordering case) never surfaced in any grep.
